decision: Design review (PLAN DESIGN): 11 decisions made, blanket auto-decision granted by user
rationale: Severity-first hierarchy, 4-color semantic scale, action-first audit, inline TTL+confirm modal, agent-health empty state, shape+text+color accessibility, CSS token mapping, verdict-first fold, mobile hide-panels, font stack complete

decision: Eng review (FULL_REVIEW): Competitive-Intel Workbench — 8 findings, all folded
rationale: Dedicated APScheduler service (not in web workers); chunk budget derived from embedding model context; pinned embedding model id+version with collection stamping; parser registry; bounded ingest concurrency; auth at reverse proxy. Greenfield, no code yet.

decision: CEO review (HOLD_SCOPE): held scope, 14 findings + 8 critical gaps, all auto-decided
rationale: Plan value rests on two unverified negative privacy claims; 3 day-1 probes gate the architecture

decision: Veil dashboard shows TWO totals: Settled on-chain and Available/spendable, with the delta and in-flight count stated
rationale: A confidential Token-2022 transfer is not instantly spendable; showing one total creates a broken-trust moment when the merchant cannot spend the full figure

decision: Veil public view renders amounts as a redaction bar lifted by the Public/Auditor toggle; one authored motion, 320ms staggered, instant under prefers-reduced-motion
rationale: Maps the encryption mechanism to a one-glance visual and gives the product thesis an emotional payload; the signature element is the interaction itself, which keeps AI-slop risk down

decision: Veil merchant reconciliation uses the recipient ciphertext, not the mint auditor key; the auditor key is an optional third-party (accountant) affordance only
rationale: The auditor ElGamal key is a single global key per mint; using it as the per-merchant read path is wrong at scale and a terrifying UX. Corrects the stale claim in docs/designs/veil-agent-payments.md

decision: Veil's "one line" claim is restated everywhere as "a one-line handler diff", with setup time stated next to it, and the first-run path is collapsed by a scaffold plus a hosted sandbox (target 5 minutes to first confidential payment)
rationale: The marketing number (diff size) and the felt number (time to first successful private payment) diverge exactly where adoption is lost; a first confidential payment needs wallet funding and owner-signed account configuration, so a <=2 min claim would be an overclaim

decision: The Veil SDK hard-refuses to serve when the confidentiality assertion fails; it must never fall back to a non-confidential payment, and every error carries type/code/message/param/cause/fix/doc_url
rationale: Extends the design review's refuse-to-reconcile decision down to the SDK and facilitator: a silent fallback to a public payment would make the product's central negative claim false while the demo still looked correct

decision: Veil display face is Cabinet Grotesk (Fontshare) with General Sans for body/UI and JetBrains Mono for data, superseding the Space Grotesk named in the plan-design-review token set
rationale: Space Grotesk is on the convergent overused-as-display list and cannot be the display voice; Cabinet Grotesk carries the archival character the redaction metaphor needs and is free for commercial use

decision: Veil uses a light paper ground for the landing page and a dark graphite ground for the dashboard, not a single theme
rationale: Light or dark is fixed by the use scene: the landing is read in daylight on a phone by someone skimming, the dashboard is watched for long stretches beside a terminal and an explorer

decision: Veil uses one red (#B4341F, lifted to #D14A34 on graphite) for the redaction bar, the brand accent and the error treatment; errors are disambiguated by code, glyph and label rather than a second hue, and red is never body text on graphite
rationale: The redaction ink is the brand metaphor and splitting it would weaken it; because brand and error share a hue, colour-alone signalling is forbidden and red-on-dark text is contrast-capped around 3.9:1

decision: Re-sweep every Veil semantic colour token to a measured 4.5:1 floor and add a dedicated redact-fill token for white-on-red surfaces
rationale: A programmatic contrast sweep of DESIGN.md found success (4.43:1), warning (3.20:1), error (4.34:1) and error-dark (4.26:1) all failing WCAG AA for small text on their own ground, and the file's own red-on-graphite claim wrong (written ~3.9:1, measured 4.26:1). Corrected values keep the hue and add headroom: light success #2C7755 4.80:1, warning #8A611E 4.89:1, error #B8402A 4.89:1; dark error/redact #DE523C 4.84:1. Because a lifted accent that passes as text fails as a white-text fill (white on #DE523C = 3.66:1), a separate redact-fill #B4341F token pins white labels to the one red that clears 4.5:1 on both grounds.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the tokens and only documenting the failures (rejected: the dashboard renders state pills and error text at 12-13px, so the failures are real user-facing defects, not theoretical). Lightening the dark-ground red further to gain text headroom (rejected: it degrades the white-on-red fill and washes the redaction bar). Introducing a second red for errors (rejected: DESIGN.md's one-red rule is load-bearing for the redaction metaphor, and label plus glyph already disambiguate).

decision: Cool the Veil paper ground from #F4F1EA to #F2F2F0 and self-host every webfont
rationale: The slop gate scored the warm cream ground as a counted slop failure on both paper surfaces. The palette was thematically motivated (a redacted statement reads as printed paper), but a neutral document stock is as faithful to that idea as a cream one and does not trip the reflex-default pattern. The move is also measurable: every light-side ratio gained headroom (muted 4.92 to 4.95, redact 5.39 to 5.43, success 4.80 to 4.83, warning and error 4.89 to 4.92), re-measured rather than assumed, with rule #D5D5D1 and tint #E8E8E4 cooled to match. Separately, all five faces were vendored locally because Fontshare's protocol-relative URLs meant the poster headline rendered in Georgia over plain http; the CJK-free total is 128KB and the mono ships as one variable file.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the cream and recording a documented exception (rejected: it is a counted failure on the two surfaces a judge sees first, and the cream was not load-bearing). Cooling only the ground and leaving the warm rule and tint (rejected: a warm rule on a neutral ground reads as drift). Continuing to load fonts from the CDN with a better fallback stack (rejected: a fallback cannot fix a first-impression FOUT on the hero headline, and self-hosting also makes the submission zip and the offline snapshots render correctly).

title: One shared token set and one behaviour file across all four surfaces, rather than four self-contained pages
detail: The design skill specifies one page per invocation and self-contained output. Four separate pages would have meant four copies of the palette, four copies of the Pretext wiring, and four places for a claim to go stale — in a project whose whole argument is that claims are checkable. Chose shared web/assets/{tokens.css,app.css,pretext.js,veil.js} plus a generator that emits self-contained artifacts on demand. Cost: the pages need the assets directory when served. Benefit: a token change lands everywhere at once, and the standalone artifacts are generated from the same sources so they cannot disagree.

title: Move the prefers-contrast:more ramp into DESIGN.md rather than suppressing the detector finding
detail: The design detector flagged four colour literals as outside the palette. They were legitimate high-contrast overrides living inside a media query with no documentation. Two options: add an inline impeccable-disable comment, or make them real tokens. Chose tokens (muted-contrast, muted-contrast-dark, rule-contrast, rule-contrast-dark) with their measured ratios recorded, so the override is auditable and a future reader can tell an intentional ramp from a stray hex.

title: State the on-chain execution gap on the product surface, not only in the README
detail: No private transfer was broadcast in this build: devnet's faucet requires GitHub auth, no funded keypair existed, and on-chain work needs SOL for fees plus rent per pool account. The tempting move was to let the dashboard's figures imply a chain read. Instead every surface carries its own provenance line naming settlement mode local-ledger-only, chain not executed, and where the privacy preconditions came from; npm run status --chain prints the same verdict by reading devnet for real. A privacy product that is vague about one boundary has no standing on the others.

title: Gitignore the key directory before the first commit, not after
detail: The repo is still pre-commit and `.keys/mint.json` and `.keys/payer.json` were untracked but not ignored, so a single `git add .` would have committed secret key material. On devnet those keys are worthless, which is precisely the trap: the habit is what carries over when the same tree is pointed at a funded cluster, and a key that has been pushed once cannot be un-pushed. Added .gitignore covering .keys/, *.keypair.json, .env*, node_modules/ and build noise, then verified with git check-ignore that the artifacts worth keeping (web/, data/, .gstack/ design evidence) are still tracked.

title: Correct the proofs-need-Rust claim, and add a command that keeps it honest
detail: The claim was wrong and load-bearing: it made a 0.0744 SOL funding gap look like a toolchain limitation. Corrected in README.md, setup-devnet.ts, status.ts, TODOS.md and CLAUDE.md, and replaced the assertion with an executable check, scripts/prove-check.ts wired as npm run prove:check, that runs 13 measured checks including the negative cases, because a proof generator that accepts a false statement proves nothing. Added a standing rule to CLAUDE.md: before writing that something is impossible or needs another toolchain, spend one command proving it.

title: Stop automating the faucet and ask for 0.0744 SOL instead
detail: The remaining gap is lamports for transaction fees and rent-exemption on 24 pool accounts. Every automated route was tried and each closed for a specific, recorded reason: the official RPC faucet returns 429, rpc.ankr requires an API key, rpcpool reports its limit reached, two community faucets return 503 and 404, and faucet.solana.com returns GitHub authentication is required. The GitHub session in the real browser cannot be moved to a headless run because Chrome cookies are keyring-encrypted. So the decision is to stop spending effort on automation and ask for one funding step, because after it every remaining action is already scripted: fund, setup --apply, status --chain, serve. Recorded so a future session does not re-walk the same dead ends.
